**Unofficial** integration, not affiliated with Indevolt. It reads your
**Indevolt** home batteries (SolidFlex, PowerFlex, BK1600...) on your local
network, through their local API (HTTP, port 8080), without any cloud nor
account.

**Never tested with a real device**: the integration was written after the
[indevolt-api](https://github.com/Xirt/indevolt-api) library that Home
Assistant uses, without an Indevolt battery at hand. The local protocol is not
documented by Indevolt. Your feedback is welcome.

## Read-only

The integration **only reads**. It never starts a charge or a discharge,
never changes the energy mode, the emergency reserve or a power limit. The
energy mode and the reserve are shown, not editable: use the Indevolt app to
change them.

## What you get

One device per battery, identified by its serial (a new IP address keeps the
device and its history, once the battery is found there: open the
**Discover** tab again, or type the new address; the old address is then no
longer read):

- state of charge (%), charge and discharge power (W), battery power (W,
  signed), state (0 = idle, 1 = charging, 2 = discharging);
- total and per-input solar power (W), AC output power to the home (W), AC
  input power, bypass power, meter power (W, sign not documented);
- grid voltage and frequency (second generation), battery and inverter
  temperatures;
- energy mode (0 = outdoor portable, 1 = self-consumption, 4 = real-time
  control, 5 = schedule), operating mode (0 = main, 1 = sub, 2 = standalone),
  rated capacity, emergency reserve, cycles and remaining times (second
  generation);
- the counters of the day (solar, charged, discharged) as plain sensors;
- **five energy indexes** for the Gladys energy monitoring: charged and
  discharged energy, AC output energy, off-grid output energy, solar
  production (with its 30-minute production, computed by Gladys).

The battery does not measure what the home takes from the grid: the
integration creates **no consumption index** to be billed.

## Requirements

- Gladys 5.2.0 or later.
- The battery on the same network as Gladys, its local API reachable on port 8080.

## Configuration

1. Install the integration from the Gladys store.
2. Open the **Discover** tab: the batteries announce themselves on the network
   (a UDP broadcast on port 8099, which Gladys listens to). Or type their IP
   addresses in **Battery IP addresses**, separated by commas (with `:port`
   only if it is not 8080), six at most.
3. Create the device of each battery from the **Discover** tab.
4. **Reading interval**: 30 s by default (as Home Assistant), from 30 to
   300 s. From four batteries on, each one is read every two intervals (every
   60 s at 30 s), to stay under the 300 states a minute of Gladys; at most 270
   values are sent in any minute, the others at the next read.

The **Test the connection** button asks each battery once for its model,
serial and firmware.

## Held energy indexes

Gladys counts every rise of an index in full. So that no fictitious energy is
ever counted, every index goes through a guard:

- a value of 0 is never sent (an off-grid index never used stays empty);
- a drop, or a rise faster than 2 kW (first generation: BK1600...) or 12 kW
  (second generation: SolidFlex, PowerFlex) on average, is **held back**: the last
  accepted value is sent again, and the status of the integration shows it.
  Neither time nor repetition confirms it;
- if it is right, click **Accept the held index** **twice**: the first click
  lists what is held and accepts nothing, the second, from 3 seconds to 5
  minutes later (a double-click counts as one click),
  accepts exactly what was listed (a jump is then counted at once, a drop
  counts nothing). If the value moved between the two clicks, it is not
  accepted: start again. Saving the configuration accepts nothing.

## Errors

- An unreachable battery is tried again after 1 minute, then 2, up to 15
  minutes, never faster than the reading interval.
- An HTTP 429 or 5xx answer pauses the battery from 1 minute to 6 hours, kept
  in `/data` across a restart.
- Saving the configuration starts the reads again at once.
- If another battery answers at an address (a DHCP change), its values go to
  its own device, never to the previous one's.

## Privacy

Nothing leaves your network: the integration only talks to the batteries,
over local HTTP. The local API of the battery asks for no credentials.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Indevolt asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Indevolt batteries | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Indevolt. It reads your Indevolt home batteries (SolidFlex, PowerFlex, BK1600...) through their local API (HTTP, port 8080), without any cloud nor account, every 30 seconds: state of charge, charge and discharge power, solar power, AC output, temperatures, and energy indexes for the Gladys energy monitoring. Read-only: it never starts a charge or a discharge and never changes a mode or a limit. Open the "Discover" tab (the batteries announce themselves on the network), or type their addresses below. Never tested with a real Indevolt battery. |
| Battery IP addresses (optional) | `string` | No | Discovery finds the batteries that announce themselves. Type the others here, separated by commas, with :port only if it is not 8080 (at most 6). Preferably give them a fixed address in your router; if one changes, open Discovery again (or type the new one): its device and history are kept. |
| Reading interval (s) | `number` | No | How often each battery is read: 30 s as Home Assistant, more if you wish. From four batteries on, each one is read every two intervals (every 60 s at 30 s), to stay within the limits of Gladys. |

## How to install Indevolt in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Indevolt appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-indevolt:0.1.3`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-indevolt](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-indevolt).

Indevolt requires Gladys `>=5.2.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Indevolt is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
